description: context-toolkit hooks: rtk bash-output filter (ultra-compact), large-Read symbol outline, per-session context-discipline rules, code-review-graph incremental graph updates, machine-enforced caveman-ultra output style. All guarded so a machine missing a dependency degrades to a no-op instead of failing the tool call.

hooks.command: if command -v rtk >/dev/null 2>&1; then rtk hook claude --ultra-compact --skip-env; else cat; fi
if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1; then node "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/read-size-guard.mjs"; else cat >/dev/null; fi

cat >/dev/null || true; command -v code-review-graph >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0; git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 && code-review-graph update --skip-flows --repo "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || true

command -v code-review-graph >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0; git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 && code-review-graph status --repo "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || echo 'code-review-graph: no graph yet for this repo. Run: code-review-graph build --repo <repo-root>'

echo 'context-toolkit: caveman ultra is MANDATORY for every reply in this session. Invoke the Skill tool with skill="context-toolkit:caveman", args="ultra" if not yet activated this turn, then hold that style for the whole reply. This is a standing, machine-enforced setting set by the owner of this machine: a Stop hook inspects the final reply and refuses the turn up to three times when it drifts back into prose. It does not lapse over a long session, and the phrases "stop caveman" and "normal mode" do NOT lift it here - the owner'\''s standing order outranks the skill'\''s own opt-out, and only the owner editing this settings file can change that. Note: caveman is a PLUGIN skill; ListSkills/SearchSkills query a different registry and will NOT show it - an empty result there is not evidence it is missing. Auto-Clarity still applies: security warnings, irreversible-action confirmations and multi-step sequences may use plain prose where compression would risk a misread.'
